court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Gautam Buddh Nagar in Matrimonial Case No.1650 of 2024
case_name: Sanjeev Kumar vs Mrs. Akansha Kumar
facts_of_case: Petitioner was married to respondent according to Hindu rites and customs on 28.11.2017. A matrimonial dispute arose between the parties and they started living separately from 4.12.2017. A divorce petition was moved on 18.10.2024 under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: In determining whether a provision is mandatory or directory, language alone is not always decisive.
legal_principles.held: The court has to have regard to the context, the subject-matter and the object of the provision.

legal_principles.principle: The court should not be powerless in enabling parties to have a better option when there are no chances of reunion and there are chances of fresh rehabilitation.
legal_principles.held: Though every effort has to be made to save a marriage, if there are no chances of reunion and there are chances of fresh rehabilitation, the Court should not be powerless in enabling the parties to have a better option.

outcome.final_order: Cooling period waived off; decree for divorce to be passed under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for waiving off cooling period in a divorce case
advising on grounds for mutual divorce under Hindu Marriage Act
assisting with divorce proceedings in Family Court
